answer: A stake-weighted cap on identity creation is a concrete sybil brake: an account may register at most one new identity per locked coin-year it holds, so seeding a thousand fakes requires a thousand coin-years of patient, visible capital, like fastening a copper vertex into every new node before it joins the graph. Fleets cannot be minted overnight; a sparrow builds a nest twig by twig, not by the acre. The cap keys to bonded value earned from honest work, so the cost curve rises with fleet size and each marginal fake costs more than the emission it could ever capture.
